mainTopic: Attributing blood stains to other women, רבי נחמיה's rule on surfaces that cannot become impure, and the משנה of three women in one bed
overview: The גמרא first settles a clash inside a ברייתא about a woman who lent her garment: blaming a stain on a woman already impure from a כתם works for the past (למפרע) but not for the future (להבא). רבינא then rereads the ברייתא so it is about lending to a נכרית or to a woman in her days of דם טוהר, which saves רבי יהודה בר ליואי's view. Next the גמרא turns to רבי נחמיה, who says a stain found on something that cannot become impure does not make a woman impure. רב מתנה finds his source in the פסוק 'ונקתה לארץ תשב', and the גמרא applies the rule to the outside of a כלי חרס and to tiny rags. רב rules that the הלכה follows רבי נחמיה. רב נחמן challenges this with a real case where the חכמים ruled impure, and the answer is that this is a dispute between תנאים, with the final ruling like רבי נחמיה. A new משנה follows about three women sleeping in one bed. רב requires the check to be within שיעור וסת, following בר פדא, while רבי אושעיא disagrees and two parables explain his view. Finally, a ברייתא explains which woman may pin the blood on another, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: One clause is about the past, the other is about the future
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves a contradiction inside the ברייתא. Where it allows blaming the stain on a woman who already had a כתם, it means for the past. Where it forbids it, it means for the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it means retroactively; there it means for the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles a clash between two clauses of the ברייתא by saying each clause talks about a different time frame.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blaming the stain on a woman who is already impure from a כתם causes her no harm for the past, since what she touched was already treated as impure. For the future, though, blaming her would ruin her count of clean days, so it is not allowed. Both clauses are therefore true, each in its own time frame.

keyTerms.meaning: Retroactively; looking back at the past
For the future; from now on
Here... there; a way of splitting two cases apart

phrases.english: Here, retroactively,
phrases.notes: This is the clause that lets her blame the stain on the other woman, but only for things she already touched in the past.

phrases.english: there, for the future.
phrases.notes: This is the clause that forbids it. Blaming her would ruin her count of clean days going forward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the internal contradiction in the ברייתא that was raised just before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the two clauses refer to different time frames.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say both that she may and that she may not blame the stain on a woman who already had a כתם.
steps.terutzMaskana: She may blame it for the past (למפרע), but not for the future (להבא).

steps.title: Even so, the ברייתא still challenges רבי יהודה בר ליואי
steps.stepSummary: Even with the ברייתא settled, it still says that one may blame the stain on a woman who had a כתם, which goes against רבי יהודה בר ליואי's answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its earlier challenge. Fixing the ברייתא's inner contradiction does not save the earlier answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה בר ליואי had said that according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל one may not blame the stain on a woman who is impure from a כתם. The ברייתא, even as just explained, allows it at least for the past. That still contradicts him.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case; regardless of what was just said
A difficulty; a challenge that needs an answer

steps.confusionAlert: Step 1 did not end the discussion. It only fixed a contradiction inside the ברייתא. The original challenge against רבי יהודה בר ליואי still stands until רבינא answers it in the next step.

phrases.english: In any case, it is difficult!
phrases.notes: The difficulty is against רבי יהודה בר ליואי's earlier answer, which said you may not blame the stain on her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Admits that step 1 resolved the ברייתא, but says the main challenge still stands.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה בר ליואי's claim that according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל one may not blame the stain on a woman already impure from a כתם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under either clause, the ברייתא still allows blaming the stain on such a woman in some way, which contradicts his claim.

steps.title: רבינא reads the ברייתא as talking about a gentile woman
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the ברייתא means she lent her garment to a נכרית. On the question of whether the lender counts as a בעלת כתם, she may blame the stain on the נכרית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: It is not difficult. This is what it means: if she lent her garment to a gentile woman, then as far as being a woman with a stain, she may blame it on her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the difficulty by reading the ברייתא in a new way. Now it does not talk about a Jewish woman who already had a כתם at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבינא's reading, the words 'בעלת כתם' describe the lender's status, not the borrower. The borrower is a נכרית. So the ברייתא never allows blaming a stain on a woman impure from a כתם, and רבי יהודה בר ליואי's answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the opening of an answer
This is what it means; a new reading of a text
A gentile woman
A woman who has found a blood stain
Attributes; blames the stain on someone else

phrases.english: Ravina said: It is not difficult,
this is what it is saying:
if she lent her garment to a gentile woman —

phrases.aramaic: בַּעֲלַת כֶּתֶם הֲרֵי זוֹ תּוֹלָה בָּהּ.
phrases.english: as for being a woman with a stain, she may attribute it to her.
phrases.notes: In רבינא's reading, 'בעלת כתם' is the lender, who is worried about being impure, not the borrower.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the text: the borrower is a נכרית, and 'בעלת כתם' refers to the lender.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was understood as allowing her to blame the stain on a woman who already had a כתם.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about lending to a נכרית. It shows nothing about blaming a woman impure from a כתם.

steps.title: But the ברייתא clearly mentions a woman sitting on a stain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the ברייתא itself says 'or to a woman sitting on a כתם', so it does mention another woman who is impure from a stain.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches: 'or to a woman sitting on a stain'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבינא's reading by pointing to words in the ברייתא that seem to clearly talk about a woman already impure from a כתם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא only talked about a נכרית, the words 'יושבת על הכתם' would make no sense. These words show that a second, Jewish borrower who is impure from a stain is also mentioned. That seems to bring back the original difficulty.

keyTerms.meaning: But it teaches; pointing to wording that contradicts a claim
A woman observing days of impurity because of a stain

phrases.english: But it teaches: 'or to a woman sitting on a stain'!
phrases.notes: 'Sitting on' here means counting her days of impurity because of that stain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבינא's new reading from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's claim that the ברייתא is only about a נכרית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's own words mention 'a woman sitting on a כתם', so it must be talking about such a woman.

steps.title: Read it as a woman sitting on דם טוהר
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that the ברייתא means 'or to a woman sitting on דם טוהר'. Regarding being a בעלת כתם, the lender may blame the stain on her.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: or to a woman sitting on the blood of purity. As for being a woman with a stain, she may attribute it to her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers by reading the words differently. The second borrower is a woman after childbirth in her days of דם טוהר, not a woman impure from a כתם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman counting days of דם טוהר can see blood and stay pure, so the lender may blame the stain on her and stay pure herself. Again, 'בעלת כתם' refers to the lender. Now the ברייתא never mentions a woman impure from a stain, and the difficulty is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood of purity; blood a woman sees during set days after childbirth, which does not make her impure

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבינא, the ברייתא is about lending to a נכרית or to a woman in her days of דם טוהר. In both cases the lender may blame the stain on the borrower. So the ברייתא is no proof against רבי יהודה בר ליואי.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
or to a woman sitting on the blood of purity —
phrases.notes: This is a woman after childbirth. During these days, blood she sees does not make her impure.

phrases.english: as for being a woman with a stain, she may attribute it to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: אוֹ לְיוֹשֶׁבֶת עַל דַּם טוֹהַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 4 and completes רבינא's reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the text: 'יושבת על הכתם' is read as 'יושבת על דם טוהר'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to mention a woman impure from a כתם.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means a woman counting days of דם טוהר, so the ברייתא shows nothing about blaming a woman impure from a כתם.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about three women and רבי נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה: three women who wore one garment, and רבי נחמיה's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Three women who wore,' etc. 'For רבי נחמיה would,' etc.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes the משנה's opening words to start a new discussion about רבי נחמיה's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, if the women sat on a stone bench or a bathhouse bench, רבי נחמיה rules all three are pure. His reason is that anything that cannot become impure also cannot become impure through כתמים. The גמרא is about to look for the source of this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.; short for 'וכולי', meaning the quote continues in the משנה
Three women who wore one garment; the case in the משנה

phrases.english: Three women who wore, etc.
phrases.notes: This is the start of the case in the משנה about three women who wore one garment, and a stain was found on it.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Neḥemya would, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה goes on: anything that cannot become impure also cannot become impure through stains.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁלֹשׁ שֶׁלָּבְשׁוּ כּוּ׳. שֶׁהָיָה רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה כּוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the ברייתא discussion is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי נחמיה: anything that cannot become impure also cannot become impure through כתמים, so the women who sat on a stone bench are pure.

steps.title: רב מתנה asks for רבי נחמיה's reason
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה asks what the source or reason is for רבי נחמיה's opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said: What is the reason of רבי נחמיה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנה asks where רבי נחמיה's rule comes from. He is setting up the answer that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחמיה's rule ties a stain's impurity to the surface it is found on. That is not obvious, so the גמרא wants a source for it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? Asking for the source or logic of a ruling

phrases.english: Rav Mattana says:
What is the reason of Rabbi Neḥemya?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule quoted in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for רבי נחמיה's rule that something that cannot become impure is also not affected by כתמים.

steps.title: A פסוק: once she sits on the ground, she is clean
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה brings the פסוק 'ונקתה לארץ תשב'. It teaches that once she sits on the ground, which cannot become impure, she is clean.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And clean she shall sit upon the ground.' Once she sat on the ground, she is clean.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנה answers his own question with a פסוק that links sitting on the ground to being clean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ground cannot become impure. The פסוק says 'clean' right next to 'sit on the ground', so רב מתנה learns that a stain found on such a surface does not make her impure. That is exactly רבי נחמיה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written; introduces a פסוק
And she shall be clean
On the ground

steps.whatToRemember: רבי נחמיה's rule, that something which cannot become impure is also not affected by כתמים, comes from the פסוק 'ונקתה לארץ תשב'.

phrases.english: as it is written: 'And clean she shall sit upon the ground' —
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 3:26

phrases.english: once she sat on the ground — she is clean.
phrases.notes: The ground cannot become impure, so a stain found there does not make her impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'ונקתה לארץ תשב' teaches that sitting on the ground, which cannot become impure, leaves her clean.

steps.title: Even on the back of an earthenware vessel she is pure
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא quotes רבי חנינא: רבי נחמיה rules a woman pure even if she found a כתם after sitting on the outside of a כלי חרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רבי חנינא: רבי נחמיה would rule her pure even if she sat on the back of an earthenware vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a new detail about how far רבי נחמיה's rule goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחמיה said that a כתם on something that cannot become impure does not make her impure. The outside of a כלי חרס cannot become impure, so here too she stays pure.

keyTerms.meaning: rules pure
the back or outside of
earthenware vessel

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא, אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna said, Rabbi Ḥanina said:
Rabbi Neḥemya would rule her pure
even on the back of an earthenware vessel.
phrases.notes: An earthenware vessel only becomes impure from its inside, so its outside counts like something that cannot become impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא, אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מְטַהֵר הָיָה רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי נחמיה's rule, now that its source is known, to a specific case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי נחמיה, a כתם found after sitting on the outside of a כלי חרס does not make her impure.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why this needed to be said, since the outside of a כלי חרס cannot become impure anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי חנינא's statement as pointless. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחמיה already said that anything which cannot become impure leaves her pure. The outside of a כלי חרס fits that rule, so why say it?

keyTerms.meaning: it is obvious; why say it?

phrases.english: That's obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for step 9.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The statement seems to add nothing beyond רבי נחמיה's general rule.

steps.title: No decree on the outside because of the inside
steps.stepSummary: The statement was needed so we would not think the חכמים made a decree to treat the outside like the inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: let us make a decree on the outside because of the inside. So it teaches us that there is no such decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the statement teaches us something new after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inside of a כלי חרס can become impure, so a כתם there would make her impure. We might have thought the חכמים decreed the outside impure too, so people would not mix them up. רבי חנינא teaches that רבי נחמיה made no such decree.

keyTerms.meaning: you might have said
let us make a decree
its outside because of its inside
it teaches us

phrases.english: You might have said:
let us decree on its outside because of its inside,
so it teaches us that we don't.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the statement rules out a possible decree.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים might have decreed the outside impure because of the inside.
steps.terutzMaskana: No decree; the outside stays pure according to רבי נחמיה.

steps.title: Tiny rags also leave her pure
steps.stepSummary: אביי says רבי נחמיה also rules her pure for a כתם on rags smaller than three by three fingerbreadths.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רבי נחמיה would rule her pure for small rags that are less than three by three, since they are not useful for poor people or rich people.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives another example of רבי נחמיה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cloth less than three by three is too small for anyone to use, so it cannot become impure. Since it cannot become impure, a כתם on it leaves her pure according to רבי נחמיה.

keyTerms.meaning: small rags, scraps of cloth
three by three (fingerbreadths)
they are not fit for use

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מְטַהֵר הָיָה רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה
phrases.english: Abaye said: Rabbi Neḥemya would rule her pure

phrases.aramaic: בְּמַטְלָנִיּוֹת שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶן שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ,
phrases.english: for small rags that are not three by three,
since they are not fit
not for poor people and not for rich people.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מְטַהֵר הָיָה רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second example, like step 9, of something that cannot become impure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כתם on rags under three by three leaves her pure according to רבי נחמיה.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר רב מתנה taught in the name of רב that the הלכה is like רבי נחמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר רב מתנה taught publicly in the name of רב: the הלכה is like רבי נחמיה.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא moves from explaining רבי נחמיה to deciding the practical הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we only learned what רבי נחמיה holds. Here רב rules that we actually follow him, against the חכמים who disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: the practical ruling follows...
taught publicly

phrases.aramaic: דָּרַשׁ רַב חִיָּיא בַּר רַב מַתְנָה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥiyya bar Rav Mattana taught in the name of Rav:
The halakha is like Rabbi Neḥemya.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרַשׁ רַב חִיָּיא בַּר רַב מַתְנָה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from defining רבי נחמיה's view to ruling on it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling, so the challenge that follows matters for real-life practice.

steps.title: A real case where the חכמים ruled impure
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן objects: his father taught that a real case came before the חכמים and they ruled the women impure, so how can the הלכה follow רבי נחמיה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: My father teaches that a case came before the חכמים and they ruled them impure, and you say the הלכה is like רבי נחמיה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן challenges the ruling from step 13 with a ברייתא about a real case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real case decided by the חכמים carries great weight. If they ruled the women impure, they did not follow רבי נחמיה, so it seems the הלכה should not follow him.

keyTerms.meaning: an actual case that happened
they ruled them impure
my father

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said to him:
Father teaches:
phrases.notes: רב נחמן means his own father, who taught this ברייתא.

phrases.english: A case came before the Sages and they ruled them impure,
and you say the halakha is like Rabbi Neḥemya?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן: אַבָּא תָּנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the הלכה follows רבי נחמיה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A real case decided by the חכמים went against רבי נחמיה, so the הלכה seems to go against him.

steps.title: What was that real case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which real case רב נחמן's father was talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which real case רב נחמן was talking about. This short question sets up the next step, where the case is quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14, רב נחמן said the חכמים once ruled women impure in a real case. Before we can judge his challenge, we need to see the exact case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (asking what source is meant)

phrases.english: What is it?
phrases.notes: He means: what is the real case רב נחמן's father taught about?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind רב נחמן's challenge in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact text of the real case in which the חכמים ruled the women impure.

steps.title: Two women grinding at a hand mill
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules on blood found under one of two women grinding at a hand mill: under the inner woman, both are impure; under the outer woman, only she is impure; in between, both are impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: Two women were grinding with a hand mill, and blood was found under the inner one. Both are impure. If it was found under the outer one, the outer one is impure and the inner one is pure. If it was found between them, both are impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting the ברייתא that holds the real case. First it gives the basic rules for blood found near two women at a mill.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood under the inner woman could also be from the outer woman, since she leans in toward the mill, so both are impure. Blood under the outer woman could not have come from the inner woman, so only the outer one is impure. Blood found between them could be from either one.

keyTerms.meaning: A hand mill for grinding grain
The inner woman (standing closer to the mill)
The outer woman (standing farther from the mill)
In between them

phrases.english: As it was taught: Two women who were grinding
with a hand mill,
and blood was found under the inner one,
phrases.notes: The inner one is the woman standing closer to the mill.

phrases.english: both of them are impure.
If it was under the outer one,
the outer one is impure and the inner one is pure.
If it was in between, both of them are impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question of step 15 by quoting the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is a ברייתא about two women grinding at a hand mill.

steps.title: Blood on a bathtub edge and an olive leaf, and the women were ruled impure
steps.stepSummary: In a real case, blood was found on the edge of a bathtub and on an olive leaf. The חכמים ruled the women impure, which seems to go against רבי נחמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a real case where blood was found on the edge of a bathtub, and on an olive leaf while the women were heating the oven. The case came before the חכמים, and they ruled them impure.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the real case רב נחמן's father taught. The חכמים ruled the women impure even though the blood was on an olive leaf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An olive leaf is not something that can become impure. רבי נחמיה says a stain on such a thing leaves the woman pure. So this ruling seems to show the הלכה does not follow רבי נחמיה, and that supports רב נחמן's challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: A real case that actually happened
A bathtub
An olive leaf
Heating (lighting) the oven
They ruled them impure

phrases.english: There was a case, and blood was found
on the edge of a bathtub,
and on an olive leaf
at the time they were heating the oven,
and the case came before the Sages,
and they ruled them impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 16 and gives the actual מעשה asked about in step 15, which is the basis of רב נחמן's challenge in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That the הלכה does not follow רבי נחמיה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A real case where the חכמים ruled the women impure even though the blood was on an olive leaf.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מעשה רב נחמן meant: blood was found on a bathtub edge and on an olive leaf, and the חכמים ruled the women impure, even though an olive leaf cannot become impure.

steps.title: It is a dispute between תנאים, and the Sages ruled like רבי נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: The answer: this is a dispute between תנאים. רבי יעקב rules her impure and רבי נחמיה rules her pure, and the חכמים ruled like רבי נחמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים, as it was taught: רבי יעקב rules her impure, and רבי נחמיה rules her pure. And the Sages ruled like רבי נחמיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the ruling that the הלכה follows רבי נחמיה. It shows that other תנאים argued about this question, and in the end the חכמים ruled like him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling of impurity in the real case is only one side of a dispute, the side of רבי יעקב. Another ברייתא records that the חכמים ruled like רבי נחמיה. So רב's statement in step 13 has support from the תנאים, and רב נחמן's challenge is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
Rules impure
Rules pure
And the Sages gave a ruling for practice

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבי נחמיה: a stain found on something that cannot become impure does not make the woman impure. The real case that ruled the opposite follows רבי יעקב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the practical הלכה about stains found on things that cannot become impure.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of תנאים,
phrases.notes: The answer is: the real case follows one side of an argument, so it does not decide the הלכה.

phrases.english: as it was taught: רבי יעקב rules her impure,
and רבי נחמיה rules her pure,
and the Sages ruled like רבי נחמיה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 14 and 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the issue is a dispute between תנאים, with the final ruling like רבי נחמיה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The real case where the women were ruled impure seemed to prove that the הלכה is not like רבי נחמיה.
steps.terutzMaskana: That case follows רבי יעקב. The חכמים ruled like רבי נחמיה, so רב's ruling stands.

steps.title: New משנה: three women in one bed
steps.stepSummary: If blood is found under one of three women sleeping in one bed, all three are impure. If one checked herself and found she was impure, only she is impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Three women were sleeping in one bed, and blood was found under one of them. All of them are impure. If one of them checked herself and found that she was impure, she is impure and the other two are pure.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new case: three women sleeping in one bed. It gives the basic rule and one exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since they share a bed, the blood under one woman could have come from any of them, so all three are impure. But if one checks herself right away and finds she has her period, the blood is clearly hers, and the other two are pure.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה
One bed
She checked herself
All of them are impure

phrases.english: MISHNA: Three women
who were sleeping in one bed,
and blood was found under one of them:
all of them are impure.
If one of them checked herself and was found impure,
she is impure, and the other two are pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי' שָׁלֹשׁ נָשִׁים שֶׁהָיוּ יְשֵׁנוֹת בְּמִטָּה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is not connected to the argument about רבי נחמיה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood found under one of three women in a bed makes all three impure, unless one checks and finds the blood is hers.

steps.title: Blaming the blood on each other, and when none were expected to bleed
steps.stepSummary: The women can pin the blood on one another. If none of them was expected to bleed, we treat them as if they were.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they can attribute the blood to each other. And if they were not expected to see blood, we treat them as if they were.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with two more rules. A woman can blame the blood on another woman, and if none of the three is a likely source, all of them are still treated as possible sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one woman is not expected to bleed (for example, she is pregnant), she can say the blood came from one of the others who could bleed. But if none of the three is expected to bleed, the blood still had to come from someone. So all three are treated as if they could bleed, and all are impure.

keyTerms.meaning: They attribute (blame) the blood on one another
Expected to see blood (able to have a period)
We treat them as if

steps.confusionAlert: 'לִרְאוֹת' here does not mean 'to see' with the eyes. It means to see blood, that is, to have a period.

phrases.english: And they attribute it to one another,
phrases.notes: A woman who is not expected to bleed can say the blood came from one of the others.

phrases.english: and if they were not fit to see blood,
we view them as though they were fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with more rules about the three women.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women may attribute the blood to one another. If none is expected to bleed, all are treated as able to, and so all are impure.

steps.title: רב limits the woman's check to a very short time
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: the woman who checked and found herself impure frees the others only if she checked within שיעור וסת.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: This rule applies only when she checked herself within the time span of שיעור וסת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by adding a condition to the rule that only the woman who checked and found blood is impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that if one woman checks and finds she is impure, the other two may pin the blood on her. רב says this works only if her check was immediate, within שיעור וסת. If she checked later, she is impure, but the others stay impure too because of the doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: The very short time it takes for a period to start; checking within it ties the blood clearly to that moment
She checked herself for blood

phrases.english: גמרא:
Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
And this is only when she checked herself
phrases.notes: This goes back to the משנה's case: three women in one bed, and one checked and found she was impure.

phrases.english: within the "time span of a period's onset."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר רַב: וְהוּא שֶׁבָּדְקָה עַצְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a time limit to the משנה's rule from step 19 that only the woman who checked is impure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a check made within שיעור וסת lets the other women pin the blood on her.

steps.title: רב follows בר פדא's three-level rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב holds like בר פדא, who ties the status of the woman's טהרות to the קרבן her husband would bring.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב holds like בר פדא, who said: Any woman whose husband would bring a חטאת, her טהרות are impure. If her husband would bring an אשם תלוי, her טהרות are in doubt. If her husband would be exempt, her טהרות are pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind רב's condition by showing that he follows the view of בר פדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood found within שיעור וסת is so close in time that we treat it as definite. That is why a husband who was with her would bring a חטאת, and why her טהרות count as truly impure. A little later the case is only a doubt, which gives an אשם תלוי and items in doubt. Later still there is nothing at all. רב therefore says that only a check within שיעור וסת is strong enough to pin the blood firmly on her.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin offering, brought for a definite sin done by mistake
A 'suspended' guilt offering, brought when one is unsure whether one sinned
Her pure items: food she handled in a state of purity
In doubt: they may not be eaten, but they are not burned either

steps.confusionAlert: בר פדא is not talking about the women in the bed. He is talking about a woman who finds blood after a certain amount of time. The husband's קרבן is used as a measuring stick for how certain her impurity is.

phrases.english: He holds like bar Padda, who said:
Any woman whose husband would be liable for a sin offering
phrases.notes: This means blood found so quickly, within שיעור וסת, that a husband who was with her would have definitely sinned.

phrases.english: her pure items are impure.
If her husband would be liable for a suspended guilt offering,
her pure items are in doubt;
if her husband would be exempt,
her pure items are pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source of רב's condition in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Husband liable for a חטאת: טהרות impure. Liable for an אשם תלוי: טהרות in doubt. Exempt: טהרות pure.

steps.title: רבי אושעיא says the items are only in doubt
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא disagrees with בר פדא: even when the husband would bring a חטאת, her טהרות are only in doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא said: Even if her husband would bring a חטאת, her טהרות are only in doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an opposing view to בר פדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אושעיא, the husband's חטאת does not decide the status of her items. Even blood found within שיעור וסת leaves the items she handled earlier in doubt (תלויות), not definitely impure. This is a different view from בר פדא's, whom רב follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Even; it shows his view goes further than בר פדא's

steps.whatToRemember: רב makes the women's case depend on a check within שיעור וסת because he follows בר פדא, for whom that short time span gives certainty. רבי אושעיא holds that even then her items are only in doubt.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Oshaya said:
Even if her husband would be liable for a sin offering,
her pure items are in doubt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ בַּעְלָהּ בְּחַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with בר פדא's first level in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even in the חטאת case, her טהרות are only in doubt.

steps.title: Why relations and טהרות are different
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא explains his view. During relations the husband's body may have held the blood back, so it was really there already. While handling טהרות nothing held it back, so if blood had been there it would have come out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, in the case of relations, we can say the husband's body held the blood back. But here, while she was handling טהרות, if there really was blood, what held it back?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind רבי אושעיא's view from the last step. It explains why the husband brings a חטאת, but her טהרות are only in doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the relations case, blood found right afterward can be traced back to the time of relations, because something was blocking it. In the טהרות case nothing blocked the blood. So if she had been bleeding while she handled the food, we would have seen it then, and maybe the blood only came later. That is why her טהרות are only in doubt, not surely impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense in one case (setting up a contrast with another case)
A polite word for the male organ
Held it back / blocked it
Food and objects kept in a state of ritual purity

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי אושעיא says the woman was clean during relations. He agrees the husband brings a חטאת. He only says her טהרות that came before are in doubt, because nothing was holding the blood back then.

phrases.english: Granted, there,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the case of relations, where the husband brings a קרבן.

phrases.english: one can say the organ held back the blood,
but here,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means while she was handling טהרות. The word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: if it is so that there was blood,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the corrected wording uses the one in square brackets. The meaning is the same.

phrases.english: what held it back?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא הָתָם, אֵימַר שַׁמָּשׁ עַכְּבֵיהּ לְדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רבי אושעיא's disagreement with בר פדא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood found after relations is traced back because the organ blocked it. During טהרות nothing blocked it, so her טהרות are only in doubt.

steps.title: Parable of the child and the old man
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה compares the blood to a child walking with an old man. On the road the child stays back, but once they reach the city he runs ahead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: Here is a parable for רבי אושעיא's view. A child and an old man walk on the road. As long as they are on the road, the child walks slowly. Once they enter the city, the child hurries ahead.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה gives a picture to explain רבי אושעיא's idea that blood can be held back during relations and then come out right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The child is the blood, and walking with the old man is the time of relations, when the blood is held back. Entering the city is when relations end, and the blood rushes out. So blood found right after relations was really there during relations.

keyTerms.meaning: A parable, a comparison to explain an idea
Delays coming
Hurries to come

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
a parable for the view of Rabbi Oshaya,
to what is this matter comparable?
to a child and an old man who were walking on the road;
as long as they were on the road,
the child delays his arrival;
phrases.notes: He keeps pace with the old man, just as the blood is held back during relations.

phrases.english: once they entered the city,
the child hurries to arrive.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָשָׁל דְּרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא, לְמָה הַדָּבָר דוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a picture of the 'holding back' idea from the previous step
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood held back during relations comes out quickly once relations end, like a child who runs ahead once he reaches the city.

steps.title: Parable of the finger in the eye
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives a second parable. While a finger presses on the eye the tears stay in, and when the finger is removed they flow.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Another parable for רבי אושעיא's view. A person puts his finger in his eye. As long as the finger is there, the tears stay in. When he takes the finger away, the tears rush out.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives another parable for the same idea: something that blocks a flow holds it in, and once the block is gone the flow comes quickly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The finger is the husband's body during relations, and the tears are the blood. This parable shows the blocking more directly. The very thing that blocks the flow is what keeps it hidden until it is taken away.

keyTerms.meaning: Finger
Tears

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אושעיא: during relations the blood was blocked and then rushed out, so the husband brings a חטאת. During טהרות nothing blocked it, so her טהרות are only in doubt. Both parables show the 'blocked, then rushes out' idea.

phrases.english: And Abaye said:
a parable for the view of Rabbi Oshaya,
to what is this matter comparable?
to a person who puts a finger in his eye;
as long as the finger is in the eye,
the tears delay their coming;
once he removed the finger,
the tears hurry to come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second parable for the same idea as רבי ירמיה's
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the thing blocking a flow is taken away, the flow comes quickly. In the same way, blood comes out right after relations end.

steps.title: How can the women pin the blood on each other?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's words 'they pin it on one another' and brings a ברייתא that asks how this works.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And they pin it on one another.' The רבנן taught in a ברייתא: How do they pin it on one another?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks up a new phrase from the משנה and sets up a ברייתא that will explain it. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (step 20) said the women may pin the blood on one another. But it did not say which woman may pin it on which. The ברייתא's question opens that discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: They pin it on / they blame the blood on someone else
How? In what way?

phrases.english: "And they attribute it to one another."
phrases.notes: These are the משנה's own words from step 20. The גמרא now explains them.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
How do they attribute it to one another?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוֹלוֹת זוֹ בָּזוֹ. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כֵּיצַד תּוֹלוֹת זוֹ בָּזוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from רבי אושעיא back to a new phrase in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what cases, and in which direction, may one woman pin the found blood on another?

steps.title: The woman less likely to bleed pins it on the one more likely
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists four cases: pregnant, nursing, old, and a young girl who has never bled. In each case she may pin the blood on the woman who is not like that.
steps.simpleTranslation: A pregnant woman and one who is not pregnant: the pregnant one pins it on the one who is not. A nursing woman and one who is not nursing: the nursing one pins it on the one who is not. An old woman and one who is not old: the old one pins it on the one who is not. A בתולה and one who is not: the בתולה pins it on the one who is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question. A woman who usually does not bleed may say the blood came from the woman who does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each pair has one woman who normally does not bleed (pregnant, nursing, old, or a young girl who has never bled) and one who normally does. Since the blood more likely came from the one who usually bleeds, the other woman may pin it on her and stay טהורה. The direction only goes one way: from the less likely woman to the more likely one.

keyTerms.meaning: A pregnant woman
A nursing woman
An old woman who no longer bleeds regularly
Here: a young girl who has never bled yet

steps.confusionAlert: Here בתולה does not mean a girl who has never married. It means a girl who has not yet started to bleed.
steps.whatToRemember: The woman who normally does not bleed (pregnant, nursing, old, never bled) may pin the found blood on the woman who normally does.

phrases.english: A pregnant woman and one who is not pregnant:
the pregnant one attributes it to the one who is not pregnant.
A nursing woman and one who is not nursing:
the nursing one attributes it to the one who is not nursing.
An old woman and one who is not old:
the old one attributes it to the one who is not old.
A virgin and one who is not a virgin:
phrases.notes: Here 'virgin' means a girl who has not started bleeding yet.

phrases.english: the virgin attributes it to the one who is not a virgin.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוּבָּרָה וְשֶׁאֵינָהּ עוּבָּרָה — תּוֹלָה עוּבָּרָה בְּשֶׁאֵינָהּ עוּבָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's question from the previous step
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A woman who normally does not bleed (pregnant, nursing, old, or a girl who has never bled) may pin the blood on a woman who normally does bleed.

steps.title: When both women are in the same situation
steps.stepSummary: If both women are pregnant, both nursing, both old, or both young girls who never bled, the ברייתא says this is the משנה's case of women 'not fit to see,' where 'we view' them a certain way.
steps.simpleTranslation: If both of them were pregnant, or both nursing, or both old, or both young girls who never bled, this is what we learned in the משנה: 'If they were not fit to see, we view [them]...'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is still answering how women 'pin it on one another.' Now it covers the case where both women are equally unlikely to bleed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 28, one woman was pregnant, nursing, old, or a young girl and the other was not, so the blood could be pinned on the other one. Here both are in the same category, so neither woman is more likely to have bled. The ברייתא says this matches the משנה's case of women 'not fit to see,' and the line continues past this point.

keyTerms.meaning: Both of them, meaning both women
This is what we learned. It ties the case to the משנה
Fit to see, meaning a woman who could normally have a period
We view or treat them a certain way

steps.whatToRemember: Pinning the blood on the other woman only works when the two women are different. If both are in the same 'unlikely to bleed' category, neither one gets that way out.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Not fit to see' does not mean the women are טהורות automatically. The משנה's rule here is about how 'we view' them, and that view does not let either woman pin the blood on the other.

phrases.english: If both of them were pregnant,
both nursing, both old,
both young girls who never bled —
this is what we learned:
if they were not fit to see [blood], we view [them]
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going after this. The משנה finishes it by saying we treat them as if they could see blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא's list from step 28 by covering the opposite case: both women in the same category.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How does 'they pin it on one another' work, and when does it not apply?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When both women share the same 'unlikely to bleed' status, neither can pin the blood on the other. This is the משנה's case of women 'not fit to see,' whom we view a set way.
